descriptors.concept_name: Framework and Scope of Foreign Contribution Regulation
descriptors.definition: The legislation governs the influx of foreign funds to safeguard national security and prevent external interference in domestic affairs. It establishes prohibitions, registration procedures, and administrative limits on utilizing foreign contributions.
instrument_references: Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010
Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Rules, 2011
Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Act, 2020
inclusion: Prohibition on public servants and judges accepting foreign contributions
Reduction of administrative expense limits
Mandatory opening of specific bank accounts for foreign contributions
exclusion: Domestic financial contributions not originating from foreign sources
Government-to-government transactions exempt under specific provisions
nearby_distinctions: Differs from general corporate statutes by specifically targeting national security risks arising from external monetary flows.

descriptors.definition: The statute defines key terms including designated accounts, foreign entities, multinational corporations, and external financial providers. These definitions determine the perimeter of entities whose funding flows are subject to statutory regulation.
instrument_references: Section 2 of the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010
inclusion: Foreign governments and their agencies
International agencies excluding specified bodies like the United Nations
Companies with more than half their share capital held by foreign citizens or entities
exclusion: The United Nations and its specialized agencies
The World Bank and International Monetary Fund
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes standard domestic corporate entities from foreign sources based on shareholding patterns and place of incorporation.

descriptors.concept_name: Prohibitions on Acceptance of Foreign Contribution and Hospitality
descriptors.definition: The law completely bars specific classes of individuals and entities, such as election candidates, journalists, public servants, and political parties, from directly or indirectly accepting foreign contributions. This ensures that persons wielding public influence remain free from external financial entanglements.
instrument_references: Chapter II of the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010
Section 3 of the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010
inclusion: Prohibition on election candidates accepting foreign funds
Prohibition on media personnel and electronic news companies
Prohibition on residents acting as conduits for political parties to receive foreign currency
exclusion: Entities outside the specified vulnerable categories that have obtained valid registration or prior permission
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes direct acceptance by restricted persons from indirect channeling of foreign currency through resident intermediaries.

descriptors.concept_name: Administrative Expenses and Central Government Prohibitions
descriptors.definition: Administrative expenses comprise operational overheads like executive salaries, utility charges, and legal fees subject to statutory caps, while excluding direct field or welfare service costs. The Central Government may restrict foreign contributions or hospitality if receipt threatens national sovereignty, public interest, or election fairness.
instrument_references: Section 8 of the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010
Section 9 of the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010
inclusion: Executive committee travel expenses and utility charges as administrative costs
Government power to prohibit receipt of foreign contributions to protect public interest
exclusion: Salaries of personnel directly engaged in training or field data collection
Direct expenses incurred in furtherance of welfare-oriented objectives like hospital doctors' salaries
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes overhead operational outlays from direct programmatic expenditures dedicated to core organizational objectives.

descriptors.definition: Organizations with definite cultural, economic, or social programmes must obtain a certificate of registration from the Central Government to accept foreign contributions. Alternatively, unregistered entities must secure specific prior permission tied to a designated purpose and source before accepting funds.
instrument_references: Chapter III of the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010
Section 11 of the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010
inclusion: Electronic applications via Form FC-3A for registration
Electronic applications via Form FC-3B for prior permission
Affidavits executed by key functionaries in Proforma AA
exclusion: Acceptance of foreign contributions without holding either a valid registration certificate or prior permission
nearby_distinctions: Contrasts general registration which permits ongoing foreign contributions with prior permission which is restricted to a specific purpose and source.

descriptors.concept_name: Banking and Account Requirements for Foreign Contributions
descriptors.definition: Recipients of foreign contributions must receive funds exclusively through a designated FCRA account opened at the specified branch of the State Bank of India in New Delhi. Additional accounts in scheduled banks may be opened solely for utilizing or keeping transferred funds without mixing any other domestic moneys.
terminology: State Bank of India New Delhi Branch
instrument_references: Chapter IV of the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010
Section 17 of the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010
inclusion: Mandatory receipt of foreign remittances at the specified SBI branch in New Delhi
Permissibility of secondary accounts in scheduled banks for utilization
Bank obligation to report receipt transactions within forty-eight hours
exclusion: Depositing non-foreign funds or domestic contributions into designated FCRA accounts
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes the primary mandatory receipt account at SBI New Delhi from secondary operational accounts maintained in chosen scheduled banks.

descriptors.definition: Articles, currencies, or securities seized due to statutory contraventions are liable to confiscation following formal adjudication proceedings. Courts of Session or empowered judicial officers handle these confiscation adjudications and determine the disposal of seized assets after granting a reasonable representation opportunity.
instrument_references: Chapter VI of the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010
Section 28 of the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010
Section 29 of the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010
Section 30 of the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010
inclusion: Seizure and confiscation of unlawful articles, currencies, or securities
Adjudication without limit by the Court of Session
Prescribed monetary limits for Assistant Sessions Judge adjudication
exclusion: Confiscation orders passed without providing a reasonable opportunity for representation
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes judicial confiscation handled by sessions courts and authorized officers from general administrative penalty proceedings.

descriptors.definition: Aggrieved persons may challenge adjudication or administrative orders by filing appeals before designated appellate courts within specified limitation periods. Additionally, the Central Government possesses powers of revision to examine records of proceedings on its own motion or via application.
instrument_references: Chapter VIII of the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010
Section 31 of the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010
Section 32 of the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010
inclusion: Appeals against confiscation orders passed by officers to the Court of Session
Appeals against registration refusals or cancellations to the High Court
Central Government powers of revision within prescribed time frames
exclusion: Suo motu revision by the Central Government for orders made more than one year previously
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes judicial appellate pathways for confiscation and registration disputes from administrative revision mechanisms exercisable by the Central Government.

descriptors.definition: The legislation outlines various punishable infractions, such as submitting false intimations, violating prohibitory orders, or unlawfully accepting foreign contributions. Convicted individuals face terms of imprisonment, monetary fines, or additional asset-based penalties determined by the trying court.
instrument_references: Chapter VII of the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010
Section 33 of the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010
Section 38 of the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010
inclusion: Penalties for knowingly giving false intimation or using fraud for registration
Punishment for dealing with assets in contravention of a prohibitory order
Imprisonment and fines for accepting foreign contributions from foreign sources in contravention of rules
exclusion: Lawful receipt of foreign contributions in compliance with statutory registration and banking mandates
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes criminal prosecution and imprisonment offenses from civil administrative compounding or asset confiscation processes.

descriptors.concept_name: Miscellaneous Powers of Investigation, Exemption, and Application
descriptors.definition: The Central Government holds wide auxiliary powers including authorizing inspection officers, investigating offences equivalent to cognizable police matters, issuing implementation directions, and granting exemptions in the public interest. Furthermore, standard statutory provisions do not apply to direct transactions between the Indian government and foreign state governments.
instrument_references: Section 42 of the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010
Section 43 of the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010
Section 50 of the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010
Section 51 of the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010
inclusion: Authorization of inspecting officers to call for documents and examine records
Police powers for investigating offences under specified authorities
Exemption powers of the Central Government for specified persons or organizations in public interest
Exclusion of government-to-government transactions from the Act
exclusion: Exemption of political parties from Central Government exemption orders
Exemption of election candidates from exemption provisions
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes routine investigative and inspection powers from broad sovereign exemption authorities granted to the Central Government.
